questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give the difference between the following pairs of transmission modes

(a) Parallel and serial transmission (2 marks)

(b) Synchronous and asynchronous transmission (2 marks)

(c) Half duplex and full duplex (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Parallel and serial transmission (2 marks)**

In **parallel** transmission several bits (for example the 8 bits of a byte) are sent at the same time, each on its own wire or channel. It is fast over short distances (inside the computer, to a printer) but needs many wires and suffers from skew and interference over long distances. In **serial** transmission the bits are sent one after the other over a single wire or channel. It is slower per clock cycle but cheaper and more reliable over long distances (USB, Ethernet, telephone line).

**(b) Synchronous and asynchronous transmission (2 marks)**

In **synchronous** transmission the sender and the receiver are kept in step by a common clock signal (or synchronisation characters) and data are sent in continuous blocks (frames) without gaps; no start and stop bits are needed for each character, so it is efficient for large amounts of data. In **asynchronous** transmission data are sent one character (byte) at a time at irregular intervals, each character being framed by a **start bit** and one or more **stop bits**, and there is no shared clock; it is simple and cheap but has a higher overhead (example: a keyboard connected to a computer).

**(c) Half duplex and full duplex (2 marks)**

In **half duplex** transmission data can travel in both directions but **only one direction at a time** (a walkie-talkie: one party speaks, then the other). In **full duplex** transmission data can travel in both directions **at the same time** (a telephone call, a modern Ethernet link).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii)

(a) Is the internet a WAN or a LAN? Explain. Name one common protocol used in LAN. (2 marks)

(b) What is the difference between a network identifier and a host address? (2 marks)

(c) What are the components of the complete internet address of a computer? (2 marks)

(d) Name 3 common ways that malware can gain access into a computer system. How can one get rid of malware? (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) WAN or LAN? (2 marks)**

The internet is a **WAN** (Wide Area Network): it is a worldwide collection of networks (many of them LANs) interconnected by routers and long-distance links (telephone lines, fibre, satellite) belonging to many organisations and Internet Service Providers, and it covers countries and continents. A LAN, by contrast, covers a small area such as a building, a school or a campus and belongs to a single organisation.

A common LAN protocol is **Ethernet** (IEEE 802.3, which uses CSMA/CD); other acceptable answers are Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) and Token Ring.

**(b) Network identifier and host address (2 marks)**

The **network identifier** (network ID or network prefix) identifies the network or subnet to which a device belongs; it is the same for all the devices of that network. The **host address** (host ID) identifies one particular computer or device **within** that network; it is unique inside the network. Example: for the address 192.168.10.25 with the mask 255.255.255.0, the network identifier is 192.168.10 (network 192.168.10.0) and the host address is 25.

**(c) Components of the complete internet address (2 marks)**

The complete internet address of a computer, its IP address, is made of two parts: the **network identifier (net ID)** and the **host identifier (host ID)**. The subnet mask shows where the network part ends and the host part begins. An IPv4 address has 32 bits written as four decimal numbers (octets) such as 192.168.10.25; an IPv6 address has 128 bits.

**(d) Malware (5 marks)**

*Three common ways in (3 marks):*

1. Opening **e-mail attachments** or clicking on links in e-mails and messages (phishing).
2. **Downloading** and installing software, games or files from untrusted or pirated websites, or visiting infected websites (drive-by downloads).
3. Plugging in **infected removable media** (flash disks, external drives), or through a network connection that exploits weaknesses of an out-of-date operating system or software (worms).

*Getting rid of malware (2 marks):* disconnect the computer from the network to stop the spread; run an up-to-date **antivirus / anti-malware** program (if necessary in safe mode) to scan the whole system, and let it quarantine or delete the infected files; restore the system or the files from a clean backup, or as a last resort reformat the disk and reinstall the operating system; then update the operating system and the software, and keep the firewall and the antivirus enabled so that the infection does not return.
